scenarios.title: Repair an IPv6 firewall that must survive startup
scenarios.summary: Reconcile running and saved rules, diagnose a provided loader, and prove the policy survives a fresh startup.
scenarios.objective: On lan0, permit TCP requests from fd69:12:23::/64 to 2001:db8:79::/64 on destination port 9443, plus their established follow-up traffic. Permit the actual established reversed replies through wan0; unsolicited inbound TCP and all UDP must remain blocked. Permit forwarded ICMPv6 type 2/code 0 from wan0 to fd69:12:23::/64 through lan0. Block other forwarded ICMPv6 headers. Keep link-local destinations on their own link. Preserve the complete supplied INPUT and OUTPUT policies and rules. Keep the supplied persistent addresses, routes and forwarding settings unchanged. Make both the running filter and saved /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules implement the complete policy. Save your intended editor draft; an unsaved draft or rules limited to the displayed clients is insufficient. Enable the provided lab-ipv6-filter.service and verify that a fresh startup loads the saved file successfully and satisfies the same traffic and full-range requirements.
steps: Run ip6tables -S, cat /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules and systemctl status lab-ipv6-filter.service. Select Request, reply and follow-up, then Run traffic test.
Use the example command picker to repair FORWARD for fd68:11:22::/64 → 2001:db8:78::/64 TCP 8443. Retain INPUT/OUTPUT. Run the request/reply and unsolicited-traffic cases.
Run ip6tables-save -f /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules, then the example --test command. Enable and restart the provided service. Choose Run startup test and Check example.

Change the editor’s :FORWARD DROP line to :FORWARD ACCEPT; Save virtual file and Run startup test. Read the failing startup policy cases. Restore the intended file or save the correct running table again, then repeat the startup test.

guide.title: Compare current and saved
guide.why: The running table filters traffic now. The saved rules file is only text until restored. The provided startup loader reads that file at the next simulated startup only when enabled. A correct current table cannot repair an outdated saved file by itself.
guide.action: Run ip6tables -S, cat /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules and systemctl status lab-ipv6-filter.service. Select Request, reply and follow-up, then Run traffic test.

commands.explanation: Inspect the current policies and ordered rules in every supplied chain.
Read saved file text; this does not load its rules.
Read loader activity and startup enablement independently.

guide.title: Repair the example policy
guide.why: Use ip6tables -S to inspect all chains and cat /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules to inspect the saved file. This capstone preserves INPUT and OUTPUT exactly. Repair FORWARD using your earlier IPv6 direction-state skills; opening every port is not a working firewall solution.
guide.action: Use the example command picker to repair FORWARD for fd68:11:22::/64 → 2001:db8:78::/64 TCP 8443. Retain INPUT/OUTPUT. Run the request/reply and unsolicited-traffic cases.

commands.explanation: Remove obsolete FORWARD rules while preserving both local chains. Rebuild the intended policy before checking.
Drop forwarded traffic that matches no explicit permit; do not use an open default to hide a missing reply rule.

commands.command: ip6tables -A FORWARD -i lan0 -o wan0 -s fd68:11:22::/64 -d 2001:db8:78::/64 -p tcp --dport 8443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
commands.explanation: Permit example clients to the required remote prefix and service port, for a new request or established follow-up.

commands.command: ip6tables -A FORWARD -i wan0 -o lan0 -s 2001:db8:78::/64 -d fd68:11:22::/64 -p tcp --sport 8443 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
commands.explanation: Permit the reversed server reply only after its earlier request; the same apparent reply without a conversation remains blocked.

commands.command: ip6tables -A FORWARD -i wan0 -o lan0 -d fd68:11:22::/64 -p ipv6-icmp --icmpv6-type 2/0 -j ACCEPT
commands.explanation: Permit exactly Packet Too Big type 2/code 0 toward the example client LAN; this is a stateless header rule.

guide.title: Save, load and prove the restart path
guide.why: ip6tables-save -f /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules copies the running table into the simulated file. You can also edit that file and choose Save virtual file. ip6tables-restore --test followed by the exact file path checks its supported syntax without applying it. A successful syntax check says nothing about whether its policy is safe.
guide.action: Run ip6tables-save -f /etc/lab-ipv6-filter.rules, then the example --test command. Enable and restart the provided service. Choose Run startup test and Check example.

commands.explanation: Copy the current table to the supplied simulated file; do not execute a shell redirect.
Validate supported file syntax without changing running rules.
Select this provided loader for the declared next startup; current rules stay unchanged.
Run the supplied oneshot loader now; read its actual load result.

guide.title: Find a persistence regression
guide.why: The supplied lab-ipv6-filter.service is a custom oneshot loader, not a universal Linux firewall service. systemctl enable records future startup; systemctl restart reads the file now. active (exited) means that one load succeeded, not that its rules meet your assignment. Run startup test begins with fresh ACCEPT rules, then applies the enabled loader and tests the resulting policy.
guide.action: Change the editor’s :FORWARD DROP line to :FORWARD ACCEPT; Save virtual file and Run startup test. Read the failing startup policy cases. Restore the intended file or save the correct running table again, then repeat the startup test.

commands.explanation: Copy the current table to the supplied simulated file; do not execute a shell redirect.

scenarios.explanation: Keep a narrow, direction-aware FORWARD policy. Save the intended complete table, validate it and enable the provided loader separately. Both current and fresh-startup comparisons must pass; an active loader can still load an incorrect policy.
hints: Compare the current destination port and reply state with the required policy. Retain the supplied local chains.
After repairing running rules, inspect the saved file. ip6tables-save -f copies the current table; saving editor text alone does not apply it.
Use the provided loader’s is-enabled/status output and the actual startup test. start of an already-active oneshot does not reload a changed file; restart does.
scenarios.simplifications: One in-process complete IPv6 filter table, supplied static persistent network/settings and fixed custom oneshot loader. No host commands/files/kernel, full Linux boot, distribution firewall manager, service ordering, dynamic interfaces, RA timing, NAT, RELATED, NDP or real TCP/ICMP exchanges. Supported ASCII file format: *filter, three built-in chain policies with [0:0], supported -A rules, COMMIT and whole-line comments. Unsupported tables, extensions, counters and shell syntax fail explicitly. Fresh startup begins with ACCEPT rules and reads the file only through the enabled provided loader. Traffic cases have separate empty simulated direction state; full policy comparison covers all supported address/port contexts. Bounded files, commands, histories, output and comparison regions.
